reason: Forcing the tag branch true routes plain non-tag/non-self refs through tag-slicing instead of returning ref verbatim at line 100, but tests only exercise 'self' and 'tag:' refs.
resolveFromGlobals returning undefined instead of the numeric value is observable, but no test resolves a 'global.'/'globals.' path so the function is never exercised.
getIncomingForPath's guard return value is consumed only by `if (incoming > 0) result += incoming`, and both `0 > 0` and `undefined > 0` are false so result is unchanged either way.
Returning undefined instead of 0 for a missing entity changes resolveToken's output, but no test resolves a path whose base entity is absent from the snapshot.
Disabling the guard lets non-state two-segment paths (e.g. self.food.value) pick up ledger.incoming['value'], which differs from the original 0, but every test uses state.* paths.
Forcing `if(!key)` true makes resolveFromGlobals always return 0, observable when a real global value exists, but no test drives the globals branch.
readNumber returning undefined breaks the tokenizer's use of numberToken.value/nextIndex for unary-minus literals, and this line is uncovered by any test.
Changing || to && in isUnaryMinus alters which '-' is treated as a unary sign versus a subtraction operator, and no test tokenizes an expression to exercise it.
Flipping `prev.type === "op"` to `!==` changes unary-minus detection after operators, an observable tokenization difference, but this line is uncovered.
Disabling the add-branch means adding an entity no longer calls markDirty(), a difference a dirty-tracking test could assert though the current suite does not.
Flipping `file === scope` to `!==` drops a file whose path exactly equals the scope (only startsWith survives), but the fs-save test uses only files nested under the scope.
slice(1)->slice(2) in normalize corrupts stripping of a leading slash (drops an extra char), but every tested path has no leading slash so the loop body never runs.
Returning undefined for the .art template changes the content written for .art files, but no test creates a .art file (only .bp/.json/.cvs/manifest are covered).
Returning undefined for the .cave template changes the content written for .cave files, but no test creates a .cave file.
Flipping `path === "manifest.json"` to `!==` makes projectRoots include all non-manifest paths; the function is reachable via projectDuplicateCommand autocomplete but is uncovered.
The handleProjectCreate catch returning undefined instead of an error result is observable, but the test suite exercises project-load/close only, never project-create.
slice(1)->slice(2) passes an empty project name to createProject, but handleProjectCreate is never invoked by the tests (createProject is a bare mock).
Returning undefined for the missing-fqId usage error changes the result, but no test calls project-save-blueprint with no arguments.
Forcing `if(!located)` false skips the not-found error and then dereferences null located.filename; no test exercises an unknown blueprint id.

Flipping `resolved === fqId` to `!==` makes locate match nearly any fqId to the first blueprint; the sole test matches via the bp.id disjunct so `||` short-circuits identically, leaving the flip untested.
Flipping `child.type !== "file"` to `===` inverts which nodes recurse, but the tree test has only a single leaf file so no nested-directory recursion is asserted.
vfs-move autocomplete returning undefined instead of [] for 3+ args is observable, but the move test exercises execute, not autocomplete.
Disabling the single-arg branch makes vfs-move autocomplete return [] instead of path suggestions, but no test covers its autocomplete.
Changing `args.length <= 1` to `<= 2` alters vfs-tree autocomplete's boundary, but no test exercises vfs-tree autocomplete.
`visible.length - 1`->`- 2` changes the last-child branch glyph (└── vs ├──), but the tree test only asserts content contains the file name, not the branch characters.
Forcing `if(existing.length>0)` true calls vfs.deletePaths([]) on an empty VFS; deletePaths early-returns internally but the extra call is observable via a spy, and this line is uncovered.
Forcing `if(args.length===1)` true makes getFileSuggestions run for 0 or 2+ args (returning suggestions or throwing on args[0]), but no test asserts the non-single-arg boundary returns [].
Changing args[0] to args[1] makes `help <cmd>` look up the wrong (undefined) command name, and this line is uncovered by any test.
